dialect.description: The shell dialect to parse the files as (shfmt's `-ln`). With `auto`, it's picked from the file name, then the shebang, falling back to Bash.

oneOf.description: Picks the dialect from the file name, then the shebang, falling back to Bash.

indentWidth.description: The number of spaces for an indent when not using tabs (shfmt's `-i`).

useTabs.description: Whether to indent with tabs, which is shfmt's default (`-i 0`).

binaryNextLine.description: Whether binary operators like `&&` and `|` may start a line (shfmt's `-bn`).

switchCaseIndent.description: Whether to indent the patterns of a `case` statement (shfmt's `-ci`).

spaceRedirects.description: Whether redirect operators are followed by a space (ex. `> file` instead of `>file`) (shfmt's `-sr`).

functionNextLine.description: Whether to put the opening brace of a function on the next line (shfmt's `-fn`).

simplify.description: Whether to simplify the code (ex. `[[ "$a" == b ]]` to `[[ $a == b ]]`) (shfmt's `-s`).

minify.description: Whether to minify the code to reduce its size, which removes comments and implies `simplify` (shfmt's `-mn`).
